transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
I feel like I’ve ruined everything in my life and I don’t deserve to be doing art or working with anyone anymore. I've just let everyone down so badly that I shouldn't even be around people.
How long have you been feeling this way, and has it been a continuous low mood for at least two years, or does it come in separate episodes with times when you feel better?

This has been dragging on for close to two years, starting the year after my divorce, and the heavy depression has been there for the vast majority of that time. It's mostly continuous, though last summer my mood lifted slightly for a few weeks and I didn't feel as sad, even though the voice and paranoia were still there.
When you mention a voice and paranoia, do you hear a voice that other people cannot hear, or feel strongly suspicious or believe things that others say are not true?

Yes, almost every night I hear a harsh male voice that sounds like my ex telling me I'm a fraud and should just disappear. I'm also completely convinced that people from the museum and my soccer circle are secretly blacklisting me online with a shared document, even though my ex and a friend keep telling me that's impossible.
Have the voice or paranoid beliefs ever been present for at least two weeks when your mood was not depressed or low?

Yes, last summer there was a period of a few weeks where my mood lifted and I didn't feel so sad or numb. But even during those weeks, I was still hearing that harsh voice at night and was completely convinced that people were secretly sharing warnings about me online.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when the voice or the paranoid beliefs were still present even though your depression was completely gone or clearly much better?

Yes, that's exactly what happened last summer for about three weeks. Even though my depression felt much better and I wasn't nearly as sad, I was still hearing that harsh voice every night and felt completely sure they were sharing those warnings about me.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when you were not depressed at all, but you still heard the voice or strongly believed the paranoid ideas?

Yes, during those few weeks last summer, the heavy depression was completely gone and my mood felt totally normal. But even without the sadness, I still heard that harsh voice every night and remained convinced they were sharing those warnings about me.
Have you ever had hallucinations or paranoid beliefs for at least 2 weeks when you were not depressed or manic at all?

Yes, that's what happened last summer for a few weeks. My mood had lifted and I didn't feel sad or numb at all, but I still heard that harsh male voice at night and remained completely convinced that people were secretly sharing warnings about me online.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when you had hallucinations or strong paranoid beliefs but no depression, mania, or unusually elevated mood at all?

Yes, during those few weeks last summer, my mood was just completely normal—I wasn't depressed at all, and I certainly didn't feel high or energetic. Even without any of those mood issues, I was still hearing that harsh voice at night and was absolutely sure people were sharing those warnings about me.

Have you ever had a period of at least 1 week when you felt unusually energized or euphoric, needed much less sleep, talked more than usual, had racing thoughts, or did impulsive things that were out of character?

No, I've never had a period like that at all. Most of the time I feel completely the opposite—just totally drained, heavy, and exhausted. Even when my mood lifted a bit, I never felt energized or high.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a prolonged depressive syndrome for nearly 2 years plus persistent psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations and persecutory delusions). Critically, the hallucinations and delusions persisted for at least 2 weeks during a period when mood was completely normal and not depressed or manic, which supports schizoaffective disorder rather than a primary mood disorder with psychotic features. No history of mania is reported.
